Content: A bank customer receives an e-mail from a sender claiming to be a bank employee. Which of the following responses is most likely to be a privacy risk for the bank customer?

Key.Rationale: Contacting the bank at its official phone number would help verify whether or not the e-mail was legitimate.

B.Choice: Calling the phone number given in the e-mail and providing the personal information over the phone

Key.Rationale: Providing personal information to a person using an unverified phone number is a privacy risk.

Key.Rationale: Performing a Web search would help indicate whether the message is a common phishing scam.

Content: Which of the following would be the best use of citizen science?

A.Choice: An experiment that requires all participants to be working in the same laboratory

Key.Rationale: If the participants must all be in the same location, there would be no need to use a distributed approach.

B.Choice: An experiment that requires expensive equipment to conduct

Key.Rationale: Requiring expensive equipment may prevent most members of the general public from participating in the experiment.

C.Choice: An experiment that requires data measurements to be taken in many different locations

Key.Rationale: If data measurements need to be taken from many locations, it would be beneficial to have participants from around the world collect the data.

D.Choice: An experiment that requires specialized knowledge and training to conduct

Key.Rationale: Requiring specialized knowledge and training may prevent most members of the general public from participating in the experiment.

Content: Which of the following best characterizes a high-level programming language?

A.Choice: A language comprised entirely of hardware logic gates

Key.Rationale: Hardware logic gates are low-level abstractions but are not part of high-level programming languages.

B.Choice: A language in which `text(each instruction)` corresponds directly to an instruction in a computer's machine code

Key.Rationale: Machine languages (in which instructions correspond directly to machine instructions) are not high-level programming languages.

C.Choice: A language that is easy for a computer to interpret but difficult for humans to interpret

Key.Rationale: A language that is hard for a human to understand would be considered a low-level language. High-level languages are generally easier for humans to understand.

D.Choice: A language that uses multiple abstractions to manage complexity

Key.Rationale: High-level languages provide abstractions that make it easy for humans to read and write programs without needing to understand the low-level details of how programming instructions are processed by a computer.

Content: A student is creating a procedure to determine whether the weather for a particular `text(month)` was considered very hot. `tt({`
	`tt(text(total)larrtext(0))`
	`tt(text(counter)larrtext(0))`
	`tttext(FOR EACH temperature IN temperatureList)`
	`tt({`
		`tt(text(IF (temperature)>=text(90)))`
		`tt({`
			`tt(text(counter )larrtext(counter + 1))`
		`tt}`
		`tt(text(total)larrtext(total + 1))`
	`tt}`
	`tttext(RETURN (<MISSING CODE>))`
`tt}`
Which of the following can be used to replace `tttext(<MISSING CODE>)` so that the procedure works as intended?

Key.Rationale: This Boolean expression evaluates to `tttext(true)` when `tttext(counter)` (the number of temperatures greater than or equal to `90`) is less than `50%` of `tttext(total)` (the number of entries in the list).

B.Choice: `tttext(counter > 0.5 * total)`

Key.Rationale: This Boolean expression evaluates to `tttext(true)` when `tttext(counter)` (the number of temperatures greater than or equal to `90`) is greater than `50%` of `tttext(total)` (the number of entries in the list).

C.Choice: `tttext(total < 0.5 * counter)`

Content: Which of the following describes how a distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attack is most likely to compromise an online store's Web site?

A.Choice: By causing incorrect information about services to be displayed

Key.Rationale: A successful DDoS attack would make the online store unavailable to users, but wouldn't cause the content of the online store to change.

B.Choice: By making it difficult for the site to safeguard customer login information

Key.Rationale: A successful DDoS attack would make the online store unavailable to users, but wouldn't allow the attacker access to customer login information.

C.Choice: By preventing customers from placing orders

Key.Rationale: DDoS attacks compromise a target by flooding it with requests from multiple systems. A likely result of a DDoS attack on an online store would be that the online store would be unavailable to customers, preventing them from placing orders.

D.Choice: By preventing the store from filling previously placed orders

Key.Rationale: A successful DDoS attack would make the online store unavailable to users, but the online store could still fill previous orders while the site was down.

Content: A media librarian at a movie studio is planning to save digital video files for archival purposes. A.Choice: Using video file formats that conform to published standards and are supported across many different devices

Key.Rationale: Using standard video formats would help ensure that the videos are accessible in the future.

B.Choice: Using lossy compression software to reduce the size requirements of the data being stored

Key.Rationale: Using lossy compression will provide only an approximation of the original video data. The full-quality original versions of the videos will be lost if lossy compression is used.

C.Choice: Using storage media that can be expanded for additional data capacity

Key.Rationale: Using media that allows for additional storage capacity will help ensure that all of the full-quality videos can be archived.

Key.Rationale: Using redundancy will help ensure that video files are not lost if a storage device fails.
